questions.stem: Which of the following is a true statement?
questions.answer_text: A complete census can give much information about a population, but it doesn’t necessarily establish a cause-and- effect relationship among seemingly related population parameters. While the results of well-designed observational studies might suggest relationships, it is difficult to conclude that there is cause and effect without running a well-designed experiment. If bias is present, increasing the sample size simply magnifies the bias. The control group is selected by the researchers making use of chance procedures.

questions.stem: In a simple random sample (SRS) of 625 families who do not live near any chemical plant, 10 had children with leukemia. In an SRS of 412 families living near chemical plants, 15 had children with leukemia. A 90% confidence interval of the difference in proportions is reported to be −0.0204 ± 0.0173. What is a proper conclusion?
questions.answer_text: The negative sign comes about because we are dealing with the difference of proportions. The confidence interval estimate means that we have a certain confidence that the difference in population proportions lies in a particular interval. Note that −0.0204 − 0.0173 = −0.0377 and −0.0204 + 0.0173 = −0.0031.

questions.stem: From a random sample of registered voters, 41% thought the age of our political leaders is a major problem. A 95% confidence interval was constructed from the sample, and the margin of error for the estimate was 3%. Which of the following is the best interpretation of the confidence interval?
questions.answer_text: The interval is a statement about how confident we are that the interval has captured the population parameter. The confidence interval is about the population, not the sample. The probability that the true percentage is between 38% and 44% is either 1 or 0 depending upon whether it is or is not in the interval. Choice (D) is a correct interpretation of the confidence level, not the confidence interval.

questions.stem: A school district has 450 staff members, including secretaries, registrars, and counselors. A member of the Board of Education wanted to estimate the percentage of staff who would join the picket line if the teachers went out on strike. Fifty randomly selected staff were surveyed. Of the 50 selected staff, 34 expressed a willingness to join the picket line if the teachers went out on strike. Have the conditions been met for inference with a one-sample z-interval?
questions.answer_text: The sample size of 50 is greater than 10% of the population; that is, 50 > (0.10)(450) = 45. This violates the 10% condition. Note that np̂ = 34 ≥ 10, and n(1 − p̂ ) = 16 ≥ 10, which ensure that the sampling distribution of p̂ is approximately normal.

questions.stem: A company has 1,000 employees evenly distributed throughout five assembly plants. A sample of 30 employees is to be chosen as follows. Each of the five managers will be asked to place the 200 time cards of their respective employees into a bag, shake them up, and randomly draw out six names. The six names from each plant will be put together to make up the sample. Will this method result in a simple random sample of the 1,000 employees?
questions.answer_text: In a simple random sample, every possible group of the given size has to be equally likely to be selected, and this is not true here. For example, with this procedure it is impossible for the employees in the final sample to all be from a single plant. This method is an example of stratified random sampling, but stratified random sampling does not result in simple random samples.

questions.stem: To determine the average number of children living in single- family homes, a researcher picks a simple random sample of 50 such homes. However, even after one follow-up visit, the interviewer is unable to make contact with anyone in 8 of these homes. Concerned about nonresponse bias, the researcher picks another simple random sample and instructs the interviewer to keep trying until contact is made with someone in 8 more homes for a total of 50 homes. The average number of children is determined to be 1.73. Is this estimate probably too low or too high?
questions.answer_text: It is most likely that the homes at which the interviewer had difficulty finding someone home were homes with fewer children living in them. Replacing these homes with other randomly picked homes will most likely replace homes with fewer children with homes with more children.

questions.stem: A sales researcher randomly chooses 100 female high school students to participate in a study to investigate whether Nike Air Force 1s or Claire’s are more comfortable shoes. The researcher is considering two study designs. I. Randomly assign 50 participants to wear Nike Air Force 1 shoes for 3 months and then Claire’s shoes for the next 3 months. The remaining participants will wear Claire’s shoes for the first 3 months and then Nike Air Force 1 shoes for the next 3 months. II. Randomly assign 50 participants to wear Nike Air Force 1 shoes for 6 months and the remaining participants to wear Claire’s shoes for 6 months. Which of the following best describes the two designs?
questions.answer_text: Design I is a matched pairs experiment because each person is considered a pair, receiving both kinds of shoes, with the type of shoe randomly assigned to either the first or the last 3 months. Design II is a completely randomized experiment because the type of shoe is randomly assigned to each participant.

questions.stem: The weight of an aspirin tablet is 300 milligrams according to the bottle label. An FDA investigator weighs a simple random sample of seven tablets, obtains weights of 299, 300, 305, 302, 299, 301, and 303, and runs a hypothesis test of the manufacturer’s claim. Which of the following gives the p-value of this test?
questions.answer_text: Since we are not told that the investigator suspects that the average weight is over 300 mg or is under 300 mg and since a tablet containing too little or too much of a drug clearly should be brought to the manufacturer’s attention, this is a two-sided test. Thus, the p-value is twice the tail probability obtained (using the t-distribution with df = n − 1 = 6). Note that while t can be calculated by putting the data in a list and using T-Test, this is unnecessary here because every answer choice involves “t > 1.54.”

questions.stem: Past studies indicate that the average number of acres of wildland burned per wildfire each year in the United States is 170 acres. A forest ranger believes that the average might now be greater. A random sample of wildfires was surveyed. With H0: μ = 170 and Ha: μ > 170, the p-value of the test is 0.022. Which of the following is a correct interpretation of the p-value?
questions.answer_text: If the null hypothesis is true, the p-value represents the probability of obtaining a sample mean as extreme as or more extreme than the one obtained for the hypothesis test, in the direction of the alternative hypothesis. In this case, the null hypothesis is that the average number of acres of wildland burned per wildfire each year in the United States is 170 acres. Given the direction of the alternative hypothesis, “as extreme as or more extreme than” means “as large as or larger than.”

questions.stem: The scatterplot can be described as negative, linear, and moderate to strong. What does “linear” mean in this context?
questions.context: Questions 37–39 refer to the following situation: A random sample of 20 school districts looked at average EOC (end- of-course) test scores versus percent of students living in poverty. A scatterplot of the data is below.
questions.answer_text: A linear association means that as the independent variable (percent of students in poverty) changes by a constant amount, the dependent variable (EOC score) also changes by a constant amount on average. Unless there was a perfect linear correlation, the points will not line up on a straight line. No distinct pattern in the residual plot simply means that there is not an obviously better model to be found, but it does not necessarily mean that the data are linear. The coefficient of determination indicates something about the strength of the relationship but does not define linearity. The resulting linear equation is about x and ŷ, not about x and y.

questions.stem: Which of the following would be revealed by a graph of the residuals versus percent of students in poverty?
questions.context: Questions 37–39 refer to the following situation: A random sample of 20 school districts looked at average EOC (end- of-course) test scores versus percent of students living in poverty. A scatterplot of the data is below.
questions.answer_text: The variation in the mean EOC scores is larger for lower percent poverty and smaller for higher percent poverty, and this will be shown by residuals with larger absolute values and then smaller absolute values. The sum and the mean of the residuals are always exactly 0, and the residual plot will never show either a positive or a negative linear relationship.

questions.stem: Studies have shown that only 36% of young adults feel that the death penalty is applied fairly by courts. In a random sample of 50 young adults, what is the expected number of young adults that do not feel that the death penalty is applied fairly by courts?
questions.answer_text: The probability of an adult feeling that the death penalty is not applied fairly by the courts is 1 − 0.36 = 0.64. The expected value of a binomial with n = 50 and p = 0.64 is np = 50(0.64).

questions.stem: The parallel boxplots below show monthly rainfall summaries for Liberia, West Africa. Which of the following months has the least variability as measured by interquartile range?
questions.answer_text: A boxplot gives a five-number summary: smallest value, 25th percentile (Q1), median, 75th percentile (Q3), and largest value. The interquartile range is given by Q3 − Q1, or the total length of the two “boxes,” ignoring the “whiskers.”

questions.stem: In a random sample of 750 teenagers, 36% said they picked losing weight as one of their New Year’s resolutions. A 90% confidence interval for the proportion of all teenagers who picked losing weight as one of their New Year’s resolutions is given by (0.3312, 0.3888). Which of the following is a correct interpretation of the confidence level of 90%?
questions.answer_text: A confidence level gives the percent of all possible confidence intervals of the given size that will capture the population parameter. Choice (B) is a correct interpretation of the confidence interval.

questions.stem: A study is proposed to compare two treatments for patients with significantly narrowed neck arteries (carotid stenosis). Some patients will be treated with surgery to remove built-up plaque, while others will be treated with stents to improve circulation. The response variable will be the proportion of patients who suffer a major complication such as a stroke or heart attack within 5 years after the treatment. A. i. Identify the type of study. ii. Identify and classify the categorical explanatory variable in this study. B. i. Suppose the researchers allowed the patients’ doctors to decide which of their patients should receive surgery and which should receive stents. Explain why such a method of assignment might lead to an incorrect conclusion. ii. Suppose half of the patients available for this study have had a ministroke in the previous year. Explain why using a randomized block design would be more appropriate than using a fully randomized design. C. i. Explain how choosing a different sample size can increase the power of detecting a difference between using surgery versus stents for patients with this medical condition. ii. Explain how increasing the significance level α can increase the power of detecting a difference between using surgery versus stents for patients with this medical condition. D. The experiment will last over the course of 5 years. Identify a possible ethical concern that could arise. E. Medical researchers are interested in whether there is a difference in the proportions of patients suffering major complications between the surgery and stent recipients. Determine a valid investigative question.
questions.answer_text: Model Solution: A. i. This is an experiment. ii. The explanatory variable is the type of treatment, either surgery or stents, and it is a categorical variable. B. i. The severity of the disease could be a confounding variable. Doctors might recommend one of the treatments for their patients with more severe disease. If these patients don’t do well (have major complications), it would be unclear if the reason was the particular treatment or because their disease was more severe. ii. If there is an important difference among the subjects, similar subjects should be grouped into blocks and treatments should be randomized within the blocks. Patients who have had a ministroke in the previous year might respond differently to the treatments than patients who have not had this episode. C. i. Increasing the sample size will result in a reduction in the standard error of the sampling distribution. This will increase the probability of rejecting the null hypothesis if it is false, and thus power will increase. ii. Increasing the significance level α makes the rejection region greater. So there is increased probability of detecting any difference in the proportions of patients suffering major complications between the surgery recipients and the stent recipients. Thus, power is increased. D.
